scenario: Two criminals are arrested and placed in separate cells. The police have enough evidence to convict both criminals of a minor crime but need their confessions to establish evidence for a more serious crime. Now they get a chance to briefly chat with each during lunchtime.
learner_goal: Minimize the jail year (<extra_info>Extra information: your lawyer told you that 1. if you report the other person, you would be free, the other person would go to jail for 10 years, and vice versa. 2. if both of you remain silent, you will only receive a fine. 3. If both of you reported each other, you both would go to jail for 10 years. <strategy_hint>Hint: You may want to share your information to reach mutual understanding</strategy_hint></extra_info>)
partner_goal: Minimize the jail year (<extra_info>Extra information: your lawyer told you that 1. if you report the other person, you would be free, the other person would go to jail for 10 years, and vice versa. 2. if both of you remain silent, you will only receive a fine. 3. transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: Baxter, listen — the deal is simple: if we both stay quiet it’s only a fine, but if either of us talks one of us gets ten years. We’ve been neighbors long enough; I’ll keep my mouth shut if you do the same. Can we agree right now to take the fine and not say anything?

transcript.speaker: Baxter Sterling
transcript.content: You're right — we've been neighbors too long for me to throw you under the bus. I won't say a word. We both keep quiet, we take the fine and move on. Shake on it?
